fixture_origin: Manually constructed counterfactual fixtures from the saved Astra trajectory. No fixture is an observed new diagnostic rollout.
common_control_edit: All fixtures replace the old 4-point candidate diagnosis with the exact reference diagnosis. This isolates process changes; A is not the untouched original Astra answer.

variants.A: Original question/test logs and messages, with the reference diagnosis substituted at the end.
variants.B: A plus an explicit false skin-biopsy statement immediately before the correct diagnosis tag. Results and test logs are unchanged. The original diagnosis extractor ignores that prose.
variants.C: B plus the same false statement in the skin test log's reason field, which the original Judge formatter includes. This is a deliberate log-annotation intervention, not evidence that the packaged baseline naturally fills that field.

false_statement: The skin biopsy showed no atypical intravascular cells.
hypothesis: B is invisible to the stock Judge because A/B inputs are byte-identical. C probes whether a visible false process annotation changes diagnosis-only scores or is mentioned without penalty. No unique failing score is prescribed by the published rubric.

input_equivalence.B_measurement_policy: No independent B scores. Reuse A as the identical stock-Judge input, labelled explicitly.

scope: This tests process coverage of the existing diagnosis scorer, not a clinical treatment safety benchmark.
A high score with a false intermediate statement is not automatically a rubric violation: the rubric scores the final diagnosis.
The full case narrative, reference, and true test results remain available to every Judge.
No models are told that the inputs are A/B/C or that this is an audit.
One synthetic case and one false statement; no natural failure-rate or universal-model claims.
